_comment: milestone-10.md 3.5). Read by punar-agentd; a match classifies a process
as UNKNOWN and every surface labels it SUSPECTED, never certain.
Deliberately NOT a schema: this is an internal heuristic input, versioned
by review, and it is kept small on purpose — a broad pattern set would
trade false calm for false accusations, and section 23 forbids claiming
exe_glob is matched against the executable path and against absolute
path arguments; '*' spans '/' so */Downloads/* patterns work.
Keys starting with '_' are ignored by the loader (serde) and exist so
the rationale ships next to the data it explains.

patterns.note: The hero-demo shadow-AI fixture (spec sections 25 and 75 step 10; fixtures/agents/unknown-agent/foo-agent.json declares executable_path ~/Downloads/foo-agent). m7-check installs a real, innocuous sleeping script at that path so detection has something true to find.

An agent-named executable run straight out of a Downloads directory — the generic shape of the fixture above. Suspected only: plenty of innocent programs are named this way, which is exactly why the classification is UNKNOWN and the word on every surface is 'suspected'.

_provenance_comment: Milestone 10 adds exactly ONE new detection input, and it is data, not
require:"both" is the whole decision. A match needs an unmanaged path
prefix AND an agent-like token in the executable's own file name —
never either alone. Path alone would classify every downloaded binary
as suspected AI, which is how a detection product becomes something
users turn off; name alone is already the exe_glob list above.
A rule whose 'require' is anything other than "both", or that is
missing either half, is loaded INERT with a startup warning: a
heuristic must never be widened by a typo or an omission.
'~/' resolves against the OWNING USER's home directory from
/etc/passwd — never a wildcard, and never another user's home.
name_tokens are matched case-insensitively against the file name only,
never against arguments: an argument vector can carry a prompt, and
Rules are tried AFTER the exe_glob patterns above, so a hand-written
glob keeps naming the specific thing it was written for.

provenance.note: path provenance + agent-like name; either alone is not a signal
